section_summary: This section (pages 161–238) of State Department decimal file 894.01B11 spans late November 1940 through March 1941, focusing primarily on reciprocal federal income tax exemptions under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Japanese government officials, military officers, technical experts, and university scholars stationed in or visiting the United States. It consists largely of diplomatic notes from the Japanese Embassy notifying the Department of State of personnel arrivals, travel itineraries, and departures, State Department reciprocal certifications to the Secretary of the Treasury, and Treasury acknowledgments directing Internal Revenue officials to facilitate tax exemptions and departure sailing permits. The file also includes interdepartmental intelligence transmittals regarding Japanese official travels, correspondence concerning a Japanese army inspector's attempt to tour American petroleum refineries, and administrative notifications regarding foreign official registration status.

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies to the Secretary of the Treasury that Dr. Tokio Sasaki is entitled to federal income tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 287 regarding Dr. Tokio Sasaki, sent to the United States for study by the Japanese Government. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government personnel in Japan and that Dr. Sasaki's service is similar in character to that of American employees abroad.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Dr. Tokio Sasaki
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim notifies the Secretary of State of the scheduled departure from the United States of Yonosuke Tanaka.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim gives notice that Mr. Yonosuke Tanaka, Assistant Local Secretary for Commerce and Industry of the Tokyo Commercial and Industrial Museum in New York, will depart New York on February 1, 1941, aboard the S.S. Kongo Maru. The Embassy states that his income is derived solely from the Japanese Government and requests that U.S. authorities be notified to ensure his tax exemption upon departure.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 5 regarding Departure of Yonosuke Tanaka

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemption for three Japanese officials stationed at the Japanese Government Railways office in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim requests that three Japanese officials whose incomes are paid solely by the Japanese Government be included in the list of officials exempt from federal income taxes. An attached list provides details for Hirohiko Tembo and Yasushi Obata, Secretaries of the Department of Railways who arrived on the Asama Maru, and Jiro Shoda, Secretary of the Board of Tourist Industry who arrived on the Tatuta Maru. A duplicate copy of the diplomatic note is included in the file.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 10 regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 10 to the Secretary of the Treasury regarding three railway and tourist industry officials stationed in New York. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions to U.S. government employees performing services in Japan and that their services are similar in character.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Note No. 10 concerning tax exemptions for three railway officials in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 10 of January 18, 1941, regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda of the Japanese Government Railways office in New York. The note confirms that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect their exemption from federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Embassy regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that income tax exemption instructions will be issued for Commander Tokiji Taira.
subfiles.from: Herbert E. Gaston, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of January 15, 1941, regarding Paymaster Commander Tokiji Taira, Inspector of Naval Fuel Depot at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York. Taking note of Commander Taira's planned departure from Los Angeles on February 9 and the State Department's Section 116(h) certification, the Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Commander Tokiji Taira

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy notifies the Department of State of a change in travel itinerary for railway official Yasumichi Tasaka.
subfiles.summary: Referring to earlier Note No. 4, the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim informs the Secretary of State that Mr. Yasumichi Tasaka received orders from his government to return directly to Japan rather than traveling via Europe. Mr. Tasaka will depart from San Francisco on February 13, 1941, aboard the S.S. Kamakura Maru, and the Embassy requests that his name be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 21 regarding Itinerary Change for Yasumichi Tasaka

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary of State Breckinridge Long informs the Treasury Department of updated sailing arrangements for Yasumichi Tasaka.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Long confirms a telephone message of January 30 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Japanese Government Railways secretaries Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda. The letter notes that Mr. Tasaka will sail from San Francisco on February 13 aboard the Kamakura Maru instead of leaving New York on the Excalibur as previously planned, and reiterates that Section 116(h) certification was provided on January 21.
subfiles.title: Breckinridge Long to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 21 regarding the revised sailing plans of Yasumichi Tasaka.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges the receipt of the Japanese Embassy's note of January 21, 1941, concerning Mr. Yasumichi Tasaka's revised departure from San Francisco on the Kamakura Maru. The note states that the information was communicated by telephone to the competent authorities to ensure Mr. Tasaka's exemption from federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Embassy regarding Yasumichi Tasaka

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for railway officials Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of January 21 confirming notifications concerning Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda of the Japanese Government Railways. The letter notes Mr. Tsuda's departure via Laredo, Texas, and confirms that arrangements are being made with the Alien Division of the Collector of Internal Revenue at New York to facilitate his departure papers under Section 116(h).
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for museum official Yonosuke Tanaka.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of January 22 enclosing Japanese Embassy Note No. 5 regarding Mr. Yonosuke Tanaka of the Tokyo Commercial and Industrial Museum. In accordance with the Section 116(h) reciprocity certification, instructions are being issued to Internal Revenue officials concerning his tax exemption before his February 1 departure.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Yonosuke Tanaka

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy notifies the Secretary of State of the scheduled departure and tax-exempt status of Mantaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim informs the Department of State that Mr. Mantaro Matsumoto, an expert of the Japanese Government Silk Conditioning House on duty at the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York, will depart San Francisco on February 28, 1941, aboard the S.S. Yawata Maru. The Embassy requests that appropriate authorities be notified regarding his tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 23 regarding Departure of Mantaro Matsumoto

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 23 regarding the departure and tax exemption of Mantaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 23 of February 4, 1941, concerning Mantaro Matsumoto of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York. The note confirms that information regarding Mr. Matsumoto's exemption from federal income tax was communicated by telephone to the competent U.S. government authority.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Embassy regarding Mantaro Matsumoto

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests income tax exemption for Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim requests that Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University, studying electrical engineering and communications in New York City, be included in the list of officials exempt from income taxes. The subfile includes a Division of Foreign Service Administration routing slip dated February 14, 1941, inquiring about the temporary disappearance of the original note, along with a duplicate typed copy of Note No. 24.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 24 regarding Kenzo Nagai with Missing Original Routing Slip and Copy

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 24 concerning income tax exemption for Professor Kenzo Nagai.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 24 of February 4, 1941, regarding Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University. The note states that a copy of the request has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect his exemption from federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Chargé d'Affaires regarding Kenzo Nagai

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Professor Kenzo Nagai.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 24 to the Secretary of the Treasury regarding Professor Kenzo Nagai. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to American officials in Japan and that Professor Nagai's studies in electrical engineering constitute similar foreign service.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Kenzo Nagai
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State formally acknowledges to the Japanese Ambassador the tax exemption request for Professor Kenzo Nagai.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State presents compliments to the Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 24 of February 4, 1941, concerning Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University. The note confirms that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to secure his exemption from federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Kenzo Nagai

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy notifies the Department of State of the scheduled departures of railway secretaries Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim reports the planned departures of Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda, Secretaries of the Japanese Government Railways in New York. Mr. Tasaka plans to sail on January 18 aboard the S.S. Excalibur via Europe, while Mr. Tsuda will depart New York on January 16 and cross the Mexican border at Laredo on January 19 to return via South America. Tax clearance notification is requested.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 4 regarding Departure of Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull confirms a telephone message of January 13, 1941, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption for railway secretaries Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda. Hull requests that departure papers for Mr. Tsuda be arranged through the Alien Division of the Collector of Internal Revenue at the New York Customhouse, and certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 4 and outlines departure tax arrangements for Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Note No. 4 of January 10 regarding the planned departures of Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda. The note states that the information was telephoned to competent authorities to secure tax exemptions, and notes that Mr. Tsuda can obtain his departure clearance papers from Room 131 of the Alien Division at the Customhouse in New York City.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Embassy regarding Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges updated departure information for Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges State Department correspondence of February 4 confirming that Yasumichi Tasaka will sail from San Francisco on February 13 rather than New York on January 18. The letter notes the Section 116(h) reciprocity certification previously issued on January 21 and thanks the State Department for the updated itinerary.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Yasumichi Tasaka and Hirotaka Tsuda

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy notifies the Department of State of the scheduled departure and tax exemption for Assistant Professor Nobutaro Ishii.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim reports that Mr. Nobutaro Ishii, Assistant Professor of Tokyo Imperial University residing in Baltimore, Maryland, will sail for Japan from San Francisco on February 28, 1941, aboard the S.S. Yawata Maru. The Embassy states that his income is derived solely from the Japanese Government and requests that arrangements be made for him to obtain his sailing permit at Baltimore.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 31 regarding Departure of Nobutaro Ishii

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 31 regarding Nobutaro Ishii and arrangements for his sailing permit in Baltimore.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 31 of February 7 concerning Assistant Professor Nobutaro Ishii. The note confirms that the tax exemption request was communicated by telephone to the competent authorities and that arrangements have been requested for a sailing document to be issued to Mr. Ishii at Baltimore.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Embassy regarding Nobutaro Ishii

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Assistant Professor Nobutaro Ishii.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Hull confirms a telephone message of February 11 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue concerning tax exemption for Nobutaro Ishii of Tokyo Imperial University. Hull notes Ishii's Baltimore residence, planned departure from San Francisco aboard the Yawata Maru, and request for a sailing document at Baltimore, certifying reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Nobutaro Ishii
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy requests tax exemption and a travel permit for Major Itizi Sugita visiting Cuba.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim requests income tax exemption for Major Itizi Sugita of the Imperial Japanese Army, who arrived at San Francisco in January 1941 aboard the Nitta Maru for travel. The note states that Major Sugita plans to depart Washington by airplane on February 18 for a brief visit to Cuba, and requests that arrangements be made for his sailing permit in Washington.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 32 regarding Major Itizi Sugita

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 32 regarding travel tax arrangements for Major Itizi Sugita.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 32 of February 10 concerning Major Itizi Sugita of the Imperial Japanese Army and his flight from Washington to Cuba. The note confirms that information was telephoned to competent authorities and arrangements requested for issuing a sailing document to Major Sugita at Washington.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Major Itizi Sugita

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Major Itizi Sugita.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of February 12 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Major Itizi Sugita of the Imperial Japanese Army. Hull notes Sugita's planned departure from Washington by airplane on February 18 for a visit to Cuba and certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Major Itizi Sugita
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for railway and tourist officials Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges State Department correspondence of February 8 enclosing Japanese Embassy Note No. 10. Taking note of the reciprocity certification under Section 116(h), the Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials concerning Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Hirohiko Tembo, Yasushi Obata, and Jiro Shoda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Tadaie Furuta during his multi-country tour.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of February 12 regarding Tadaie Furuta, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commissioner in New York. The letter notes Furuta's upcoming travel from Miami to Cuba on February 23, subsequent departure on February 27 for Panama and Mexico, and final sailing from Los Angeles on March 10, confirming that Section 116(h) instructions have been issued.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Tadaie Furuta

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for Assistant Professor Goro Fukuyama of Hokkaido Imperial University.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Mr. Goro Fukuyama, Assistant Professor of Hokkaido Imperial University residing in Berkeley, California, be granted tax exemption. The note states that Fukuyama arrived at San Francisco in June 1940 aboard the Asama Maru to study forest technology and that his compensation is paid solely by the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 38 regarding Goro Fukuyama

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 38 regarding tax exemption for Goro Fukuyama.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 38 of February 19 concerning Assistant Professor Goro Fukuyama. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that a copy has been transmitted to competent U.S. government authorities to ensure tax exemption on Fukuyama's official compensation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Goro Fukuyama

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Goro Fukuyama.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull encloses a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 38 regarding Assistant Professor Goro Fukuyama of Hokkaido Imperial University. Hull certifies to the Secretary of the Treasury under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants reciprocal exemptions and that Fukuyama's forest technology studies are comparable in character to foreign services performed by U.S. employees.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Goro Fukuyama
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Assistant Military Engineer Rokuro Nagao in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Mr. Rokuro Nagao be included in the list of Japanese officials exempt from income taxes. The note states that Nagao was assigned to the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office in New York City as an Assistant Military Engineer, having arrived at San Francisco on January 1, 1941, aboard the Tatuta Maru, with his income derived entirely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 40 regarding Rokuro Nagao

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 40 concerning tax exemption for Rokuro Nagao.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 40 of February 19 regarding Assistant Military Engineer Rokuro Nagao. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government to effect the tax exemption on Nagao's compensation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Rokuro Nagao

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Rokuro Nagao.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Embassy Note No. 40 regarding Assistant Military Engineer Rokuro Nagao of the Imperial Japanese Army Inspector's Office in New York. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, stating that Japan grants an equivalent exemption to U.S. government employees in Japan.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Rokuro Nagao
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State of the scheduled departure and tax clearance for Takehiko Uyeda.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador reports that Mr. Takehiko Uyeda, Secretary to the Department of Agriculture and Forestry in Tokyo assigned to the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York, will depart from San Francisco on March 13, 1941, aboard the Asama Maru. The Embassy requests that appropriate authorities be notified so that Uyeda may obtain his sailing permit in New York.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 39 regarding Departure of Takehiko Uyeda

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Takehiko Uyeda.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of February 21 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Takehiko Uyeda of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. Hull notes Uyeda's upcoming departure from San Francisco aboard the Asama Maru, his request to obtain a sailing document in New York, and certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Takehiko Uyeda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 39 regarding departure arrangements for Takehiko Uyeda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 39 of February 19 concerning Takehiko Uyeda. The note confirms that information was telephoned to competent U.S. authorities to ensure tax exemption and that arrangements have been requested for issuing a sailing document to Mr. Uyeda in New York.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Takehiko Uyeda

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Assistant Professor Nobutaro Ishii.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of February 14 confirming oral notice regarding Assistant Professor Nobutaro Ishii of Tokyo Imperial University. The Treasury notes Ishii's residence in Baltimore, departure on February 28 from San Francisco, and request for a sailing document at Baltimore, confirming that appropriate Section 116(h) instructions will be issued.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Nobutaro Ishii

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Mantaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of February 10 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Mantaro Matsumoto of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. Hull notes Matsumoto's planned departure from San Francisco on February 28 aboard the Yawata Maru, his request for a sailing document in New York, and certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Mantaro Matsumoto
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Mantaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of February 15 regarding Mantaro Matsumoto of the Silk Conditioning House and Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. The letter confirms that in view of the State Department's reciprocity certification under Section 116(h), appropriate instructions are being issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding his departure and tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Mantaro Matsumoto

subfiles.about: The Japanese Embassy details the multi-country travel itinerary and requests sailing permits for Tadaie Furuta.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim reports that Mr. Tadaie Furuta, Secretary to the Japanese Financial Commissioner in New York, will leave Miami on February 23 for Cuba, return to Miami on February 27 before traveling to Panama and Mexico, and finally sail from Los Angeles for Japan on March 10 aboard the Asama Maru. The Embassy requests that authorities arrange sailing permits for him at Miami and Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 25 regarding Travel Plans of Tadaie Furuta

subfiles.about: The Department of State forwards confidential information regarding Tadaie Furuta's travels to Military Intelligence.
subfiles.summary: In a confidential communication, the Department of State transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 25 of February 5, 1941, regarding the travel plans of Tadaie Furuta to the Military Intelligence Division of the War Department. The transmittal notes that identical information has also been forwarded to the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Office of Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.title: Department of State Transmission to Military Intelligence Division regarding Tadaie Furuta

subfiles.about: The Department of State transmits confidential information on Tadaie Furuta's travel itinerary to Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.summary: In a confidential memorandum addressed to Captain Nixon of the Office of Naval Intelligence, the Department of State forwards a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 25 detailing Tadaie Furuta's upcoming travel through the Caribbean and Central America. The memorandum notes that copies have also been provided to the FBI and the War Department's Military Intelligence Division.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum for Captain Nixon regarding Tadaie Furuta
subfiles.to: Captain Nixon, Office of Naval Intelligence

subfiles.about: G. S. Walden encloses an incoming Mitsui & Co. cable concerning Colonel Takahisa Nakamura's desire to inspect U.S. oil refineries.
subfiles.summary: G. S. Walden writes to Alger Hiss following up on a telephone conversation regarding an inquiry from Mr. Miyazaki, confirming advice that any inspection request must be handled through the Japanese Embassy and the State Department. An attached incoming cablegram from Mitsui & Co. in San Francisco reveals that Colonel Takahisa Nakamura, Japanese military inspector at New York, sought to inspect oil refineries in Brooklyn, Buffalo, and Texas before departing the United States.
subfiles.title: G. S. Walden to Alger Hiss regarding Colonel Takahisa Nakamura's Request to Inspect Oil Refineries
subfiles.to: Alger Hiss, Assistant to Adviser on Political Relations, Department of State

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Professor Kenzo Nagai.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of February 19 enclosing Japanese Embassy Note No. 24 regarding Professor Kenzo Nagai of Tohoku Imperial University. Based on the State Department's Section 116(h) reciprocity certification, instructions are being issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding Nagai's income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Kenzo Nagai

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption instructions for Major Itizi Sugita.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges State Department correspondence of February 18 confirming telephone notice regarding Major Itizi Sugita of the Imperial Japanese Army. The Treasury acknowledges his upcoming travel to Cuba and confirms that Section 116(h) instructions have been issued to Internal Revenue officials for his departure documentation.
subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of the Treasury to Secretary of State regarding Major Itizi Sugita

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Language Officer Lieutenant Commander Sadayosi Nakayama.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Lieutenant Commander Sadayosi Nakayama, a Language Officer assigned to the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office in Washington, D.C., to study English, be granted exemption from income taxes. The note states that Commander Nakayama arrived at San Francisco on February 16, 1941, aboard the Kamakura Maru and receives his compensation solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 44 regarding Lieutenant Commander Sadayosi Nakayama

subfiles.about: The Department of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Lieutenant Commander Sadayosi Nakayama is automatically exempt as an embassy employee.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 44 of February 24 regarding Lieutenant Commander Sadayosi Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office. The note explains that because Commander Nakayama will be exempt from federal income tax as an employee of the Embassy, no administrative action by the Department of State is required.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Lieutenant Commander Sadayosi Nakayama

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador reports the scheduled departure and requests tax clearance for Kiyoshi Murai.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Mr. Kiyoshi Murai, Technical Expert of the Japanese Government Raw Silk Conditioning House assigned to the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York, will depart New York on March 5, 1941, aboard the Asozan Maru. The Embassy requests that his name be brought to the attention of appropriate authorities for tax clearance.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 42 regarding Departure of Kiyoshi Murai

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Kiyoshi Murai.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull confirms a telephone message of February 28 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Kiyoshi Murai of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau. Hull notes Murai's departure from New York on March 5 aboard the Asozan Maru and certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Kiyoshi Murai
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 42 regarding departure arrangements for Kiyoshi Murai.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Japanese Embassy Note No. 42 of February 24 regarding Kiyoshi Murai of the Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau in New York. The note states that the substance of the request was telephoned to competent U.S. authorities to facilitate Murai's federal income tax exemption prior to his departure on the Asozan Maru.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Kiyoshi Murai

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for Dr. Kentaro Shimizu of Tokyo Imperial University.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Dr. Kentaro Shimizu, an Assistant of Tokyo Imperial University residing in New York City, be included in the list of officials exempt from income taxes. The note states that Dr. Shimizu arrived at Seattle in May 1940 aboard the Heian Maru to study neurological surgery and is supported entirely by the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 51 regarding Dr. Kentaro Shimizu

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Dr. Kentaro Shimizu.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 51 to the Secretary of the Treasury concerning Dr. Kentaro Shimizu. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. personnel and that Dr. Shimizu's neurological surgery studies represent comparable foreign service.
subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Henry Morgenthau, Jr., regarding Dr. Kentaro Shimizu
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 51 regarding tax exemption for Dr. Kentaro Shimizu.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 51 of February 26 regarding Dr. Kentaro Shimizu of Tokyo Imperial University. The note confirms that a copy has been transmitted to competent U.S. authorities with a view to granting Dr. Shimizu exemption from federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Dr. Kentaro Shimizu

subfiles.about: The Department of State requests that Dr. Kentaro Shimizu complete a Foreign Official Status Notification form.
subfiles.summary: Referring to Embassy Note No. 51 of February 26 concerning Dr. Kentaro Shimizu, the Secretary of State cites the Department's circular note of December 16, 1940. The note requests that Dr. Shimizu complete a Foreign Official Status Notification form in duplicate and submit it through the Embassy to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to Japanese Ambassador regarding Status Form for Dr. Kentaro Shimizu

subfiles.about: Nathaniel P. Davis acknowledges Hisashi Nihei's letter regarding departure documentation.
subfiles.from: Nathaniel P. Davis, Chief, Division of Foreign Service Administration, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Nathaniel P. Davis, Chief of the Division of Foreign Service Administration, acknowledges receipt of a letter from Hisashi Nihei of Osaka Syosen Kaisya in New York regarding his desire to obtain departure clearance. Davis informs Nihei that the Bureau of Internal Revenue has received a copy of his inquiry and that an appropriate direct reply is being prepared.
subfiles.title: Nathaniel P. Davis to Hisashi Nihei regarding Departure Clearance
